Subject: Escrowed credit amortization & ramp terms for FinTech Corp

Emma —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Per our conversation, attached is a clean term sheet that frames the multi-year prepay as an escrowed credit that amortizes monthly (drawdown) against usage. Key items I wanted to call out up front:

- Structure: 36-month agreement with annual prepay tranches (Year 1, Year 2, Year 3) held in escrow. Credits are consumed monthly based on invoice-level usage, with monthly burn-down reporting.
- Discounts: 18% effective discount on Year 1 prepaid dollars; 14% Year 2; 10% Year 3 (illustrative — negotiable based on commitment).
- Ramp / true-up: We provide a 9-month ramp allowance where credits are applied at 50% burn rate for forecast-to-actual mismatch, then full drawdown thereafter. Quarterly true-ups allow credits to be rebalanced between tranches.
- Refund / termination: If FinTech terminates early, remaining escrow balance is refundable less an unwind fee (1.5% of remaining balance) unless you elect a conversion to open-credit at a reduced discount schedule.
- Reporting & controls: Monthly export (CSV) of token/embedding usage by route; Team-level caps and per-route prioritization available on Dedicated plans.

I attached a draft schedule with a worked example using your June–Dec forecast. The file also shows an amortization table (monthly drawdown) and a simple waterfall for overage billing.

Next steps: if this aligns with procurement’s expectations, we can: (1) lock the discount tiers and sign the term sheet, (2) wire Year 1 prepay into escrow, (3) provision Dedicated capacity and share the consumption dashboard.

Would you prefer we set up a short call with finance/legal to walk the escrow and refund language?

Thanks,

Lauren —

Thanks for routing. Quick answers / suggested language below — happy to jump on the 9–11AM PT slot tomorrow:

1) Escrow custodian: We have two approved patterns. For strategic customers we typically use a third-party trust (Stripe Treasury / custodian agreement) and reference the custodian in the term sheet. Wording: "Prepaid funds will be held in a third-party custodian account (designated escrow) under an agreement with [Custodian]. Redwood will have no unilateral right to transfer escrowed funds except as provided in this Agreement."

2) Accounting treatment: From Redwood’s perspective, prepaid funds held in escrow are recognized as deferred revenue that amortizes to revenue as services are delivered or as credits are consumed. Suggested controller language (short): "Prepaid customer funds held in a designated escrow account shall be treated as deferred revenue on Redwood’s balance sheet and recognized as revenue in proportion to usage, consistent with ASC 606 guidance." (Recommend legal confirm.)

3) Ramp spike behavior: Proposed operational rule — credits in escrow are applied immediately to usage. The 9-month ramp allowance reduces the effective consumption rate for the purposes of discount calculation (i.e., during ramp months, only 50% of the forecast delta counts toward accelerated drawdown). Practically: if month 3 shows 2x forecast, credits will cover usage until escrow is exhausted; however, overage beyond available credits will be billed at standard list rates. We should call this out with a worked example in the CSV.

4) Refund timing: Standard processing is 30–45 business days after termination acceptance and final audit of usage. We retain the unwind fee (1.5%) and any outstanding invoices.

5) Suggested negotiation levers for sales: include an opt-in conversion at termination to move remaining balance to an open credit pool at a 5% haircut rather than refund (reduces cash churn). Also offer an annual top-up discount (2% additional discount on Year 2+ if they prepay within 60 days of anniversary).

I attached a quick amortization excerpt showing sample monthly drawdown for the Year 1 $2M prepay with the 9-month ramp applying 50% of forecast delta.
